post.caption: Berlin iron jewelry looked like black lace. In 1813, Princess Marianne asked women to give gold for iron. Donors got iron rings inscribed with a patriotic German motto. The Royal Iron Foundry in Berlin opened in 1804. Berlin and Gleiwitz, now Gliwice in Poland, both cast iron jewelry. Molten iron was poured into fine molds, usually described as sand. A black lacquer finish kept the iron from rusting. Donors wore it with pride, and blackened iron became fashionable. Later designs copied Gothic cathedral windows in miniature. Rare pieces combine blackened iron with polished steel. The same Berlin foundry cast the iron Kreuzberg monument, dedicated in 1821.
